Other key alternatives — e.g., diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis — typically do *not* cause prominent unintentional weight loss in isolation; they are associated with comorbidities (e.g., retinopathy, neuropathy, hypertension) not mentioned here. Amyloidosis or vasculitis (e.g., ANCA-associated) are possible but less likely without proteinuria, hematuria, or active urinary sediment (all pending), or constitutional signs (absent per summary). The combination of *unexplained weight loss + anemia + small echogenic kidneys + no obvious cause* strongly prioritizes malignancy screening — and myeloma is the most common paraprotein-mediated disorder causing this triad.
